title: Determinants of psychopharmacological multimedication in unipolar and bipolar depression
summary:
Combined treatment with numerous medications (polypharmacy) is often associated with side effects and often leads to further treatment and possibly hospitalization. The willingness to continue taking the medication is usually low. The following definition of polypharmacy is used for this study: ≥ 3 disease-specific, fixed medications at the time of discharge. On-demand medication and fixed sleep medication are not taken into account. 
Questions: 
1) What is the percentage of psychopharmacological polypharmacy in the diagnoses of unipolar depression and bipolar depression.
2) Are there determinants for psychopharmacological polypharmacy at the time of discharge in psychiatric inpatients with unipolar depression and bipolar depression?
Retrospective data collection of patients with a main diagnosis of unipolar depression (group 1) or bipolar depression (group 2) who were in inpatient or day-care psychiatric treatment in 2022 or 2023. The data is evaluated pseudonymously; publications are only made on the basis of anonymized data.
conditions: Unipolar depression and bipolar depression (F32.X, F33.X, F31.3, F31.4, F31.5)
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Main diagnosis on discharge unipolar depression or bipolar depression (ICD 10 F32.X, F33.X, F31.3, F31.4, F31.5)
Day clinic treatment /full inpatient treatment
Survey period 2022-2023
Exclusion criteria:
none
